theorems.title: Finite-Horizon Certificate Validity
theorems.scope_note: Defended as a finite-horizon runtime certificate theorem; if the reachable tube remains inside the safe set, releases governed by the certificate remain safe until expiry or an invalidating event.
theorems.weakest_step: The theorem is finite-horizon and runtime-object scoped; it does not claim universal plant-time safety beyond the certified tube or after invalidating evidence.

theorems.title: Certificate Expiration Bound

theorems.weakest_step: The defended row depends on keeping the delta-aware helper canonical and not silently widening the theorem surface back to legacy no-delta semantics.

theorems.remediation_detail: Keep the no-delta legacy semantics out of the theorem-facing API and preserve the explicit first-passage side conditions.

theorems.title: Feasible Fallback Existence
theorems.scope_note: Defended as a battery-specific piecewise fallback theorem: safe hold on the interior, safe landing near the boundary, and fail-closed infeasibility otherwise.
theorems.weakest_step: The theorem is battery-specific and only defended for the piecewise hold-or-safe-landing fallback surface implemented by the runtime.
theorems.code_correspondence_detail: The validator now certifies the piecewise T7 surface directly: interior hold, boundary recovery by safe landing, and fail-closed infeasibility.
theorems.remediation_detail: Preserve the piecewise hold-or-safe-landing scope and do not generalize T7 into a cross-domain transfer theorem.

theorems.title: Graceful Degradation Dominance with Useful Work
theorems.scope_note: Defended as paired-trace dominance; ORIUS weakly reduces true-state violations versus blind persistence while preserving a declared fraction of useful work.
typed_obligations: Paired graceful and uncontrolled policies are evaluated on the same admissible fault trace.
The useful-work threshold lambda is declared before evaluating dominance.
theorems.weakest_step: The theorem proves a two-objective partial order on paired traces; it does not claim that shutdown is operationally equivalent to graceful degradation.
theorems.code_correspondence_detail: The policy frontier helper compares Blind, Shutdown, Ramp, and ORIUS policies with safety and useful-work gates.
theorems.remediation_detail: Preserve the useful-work threshold so immediate shutdown cannot satisfy T8 merely by being safe.

theorems.title: Impossibility of Quality-Ignorant Mandatory Release
theorems.scope_note: Defended as a mandatory-release impossibility theorem; when an observation ambiguity class has empty common safe core, no observation-only controller can guarantee true-state safety for every latent state in that class; domain discharge is evidence, not an extra hidden assumption.
typed_obligations: Mandatory release policy depends only on the observation.
The observation ambiguity class has empty common safe core.
theorems.weakest_step: The impossibility applies only to mandatory observation-only release; optional abstention, fallback, uncertainty expansion, or denial of release are outside the lower-bound class.
theorems.code_correspondence_detail: The ambiguity helpers build ambiguity classes, compute common safe cores, and find mandatory-release counterexamples.
theorems.remediation_detail: Keep T9 tied to empty-safe-core witnesses and do not restate it as a universal impossibility for policies allowed to abstain or fail closed; domain discharge is evidence, not an extra hidden assumption.

theorems.title: Boundary-Indistinguishability Lower Bound
theorems.scope_note: Defended as a two-state boundary lower bound; observation-only mandatory release has worst-case risk at least (1-epsilon)/2 when two boundary states have disjoint safe-action sets and observation laws within TV epsilon; domain discharge is evidence, not an extra hidden assumption.
typed_obligations: Two latent boundary states induce observation distributions within the stated TV radius.
The two state-conditioned safe-action sets are disjoint.
theorems.weakest_step: The result is a two-hypothesis lower bound, not a sharp global frontier for arbitrary policies or observation models.
theorems.code_correspondence_detail: The boundary-indistinguishability helper estimates total variation and evaluates the exact two-state lower-bound curve.
theorems.remediation_detail: Do not describe T10 as a full minimax frontier; the scoped minimax row is T_minimax and still lacks a global optimality claim; domain discharge is evidence, not an extra hidden assumption.

theorems.scope_note: Flagship lemma in the runtime monotonicity law suite: enlarging the uncertainty set can only shrink the common safe-action set.

theorems.remediation_detail: Keep L2 as set antitonicity and do not restore the old capacity-proxy bridge as a defended theorem.

theorems.title: L3: Intervention Threshold

typed_obligations: Candidate action membership is checked against the common safe core.

theorems.code_correspondence_detail: The runtime law helper checks when a candidate lies outside the common safe core.
theorems.remediation_detail: Keep L3 as the runtime intervention threshold and do not revive the old critical-capacity theorem wording.

theorems.title: T11_Byzantine: Byzantine-Robust Reliability Aggregation
theorems.scope_note: Defended robust reliability aggregation theorem for bounded scores with at most b<n/2 Byzantine channels and honest scores in a radius-rho interval.
typed_obligations: Reliability sub-scores lie in [0,1].
Byzantine budget b is strictly less than n/2.
Honest scores lie in an interval of width 2rho centered at the honest score.
theorems.weakest_step: The theorem makes no guarantee when b>=n/2 or when honest-channel concentration fails.
theorems.code_correspondence_detail: The robust OQE helpers implement trimmed mean, median-of-means, adversarial channel injection, and honest-interval error checks.
theorems.remediation_detail: Preserve the b<n/2 condition and honest-interval hypothesis in all manuscript-facing statements.

theorems.title: T_stale_decay: Stale-Hold Uncertainty Growth
theorems.scope_note: Defended stale-hold uncertainty theorem: under bounded latent drift, stale observation radius grows conservatively as r_t+Ls.
typed_obligations: No fresh observation arrives for s steps.
Latent state drift is bounded by L per step.
Certified release at the stale step is checked over the enlarged set.
theorems.weakest_step: The theorem is bounded-drift containment, not a claim that an exponential reliability decay schedule is a physical law.
theorems.code_correspondence_detail: The stale-hold helpers compute linear radius growth and certificate-horizon expiry under stale intervals.
theorems.remediation_detail: Preserve the bounded-drift stale-hold radius statement and avoid deriving physical sensing laws from design schedules.

theorems.title: T_minimax: Finite Ambiguity-Class Minimax Lower Bound
theorems.scope_note: Scoped flagship theorem for finite two-state boundary ambiguity classes; it is a lower bound only and does not claim global minimax optimality.

theorems.weakest_step: This is a scoped lower bound over a finite ambiguity class; no matching ORIUS upper bound is asserted as global optimality.
theorems.code_correspondence_detail: The minimax helper delegates to the two-state boundary lower-bound calculator and exposes optional ORIUS coverage upper bounds separately.
theorems.remediation_detail: Do not use the word optimal unless a matching upper bound is added for the same policy and distribution class.

theorems.title: T_sensor_converse: Sensor Necessity Under Adapter Semantics
theorems.scope_note: Defended sensor-necessity theorem under adapter semantics: if an omitted latent coordinate changes safe-action sets to disjoint cores, observation-only mandatory release cannot certify safety without sensing, expansion, fallback, or denial.
typed_obligations: Safe-action map depends on the omitted latent coordinate.
Two states differing only in that coordinate have disjoint safe-action sets.
Policy class is observation-only mandatory release.

theorems.code_correspondence_detail: Sensor ablation helpers remove observation keys, recompute safe cores, and identify critical sensor drops.
theorems.remediation_detail: Preserve the missing-coordinate and disjoint-safe-core hypotheses; do not claim every low-quality sensor is universally necessary.
